lines.text: Hi, I'm Sindy! Today, we rehearse a change before production gets it.
Want to try a new scheduler setting, or the next Slurm release? Production is the last place to find out what breaks.
All you need is sind and Docker. We'll build a throwaway cluster that runs your change instead.
Say you run a Slurm site, and you want to test a new scheduler setting.
Production runs one Slurm release line, and the next line is already out.
So you rehearse both on your laptop, in a cluster you can throw away.
First, a quick refresher. slurm.conf tells the Slurm daemons and commands what the cluster looks like.
SlurmctldHost names the controller. NodeName lines describe the compute nodes, and a partition line groups them into a queue for jobs.
An include line pulls in another file. sind keeps its nodes and partition in a file of their own, sind nodes dot conf.
sind rewrites that file when you add or remove workers, and leaves slurm.conf alone.
Your change goes into the slurm section of the cluster config. Its main key extends slurm.conf.
Here, main is a map. Each name becomes a fragment file, like scheduling, with the backfill settings you want to test.
sind writes an include line for each fragment, just before the include of its nodes file.
Only the first block is fixed, because sind depends on it.
Everything below it is a default: a value you set in main replaces the one sind writes.
sind writes slurm.conf only once, at creation. To try another value, edit it on the controller, or create the cluster again.
Now the release. Every supported Slurm release line has its own official node image.
The year and month tag moves to each new patch of its line. A tag with the patch number stays on one release.
Set the tag production runs as the default image, and every node runs that line.
For the next release, switch to the newer line and create the cluster again.
Let's build it. Run sind create cluster with the config flag. The double v flag adds debug lines, so we can watch every step.
The info lines name the cluster, and the Slurm version sind found in the image.
The debug lines show sind waiting for the nodes, then enabling slurmctld and slurmd.
That's the release line production runs, now with your setting.
When the rehearsal is over, sind delete cluster throws it all away.
Under the hood, sind runs the controller image once, in a throwaway container, and asks slurmctld for its version.
It stores the version as a label on every node container, and the Slurm column of sind get clusters shows it.
Add workers from another image later, and sind refuses them unless the versions match. slurmd must not be newer than slurmctld.
To sum up: the slurm section carries your change, the image tag picks the release, and delete cluster throws it away.
Rehearsal done, and production never noticed! Next up: failure drills. See you there!
